answer: A farm has to staff both sides of that split with keys it controls, thus it pays the saffron fee twice and still divides one payout. Because the trellis ledger attributes every share, the shale audit shows the split and self-attestation collapses into a single position. Only 80% of a settled reward goes to the author; the rest is split among the identities that attested to it, so authoring alone does not pay. That is 35 dollars per alias. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
